chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abi al-Sabbah al-Kinani, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
Concerning a man who dies while traveling in a land where none are with him except women, he said:

He is to be buried and not given ghusl. And a woman who is among men is in that same situation: she is to be buried and not given ghusl, unless her husband is with her. If her husband is with her, he gives her ghusl from over the garment, and he pours the water over her by pouring, and he must not look at her 'awrah. And his wife gives him ghusl if he dies. And the woman is not in the same position as men; the woman is worse in appearance when she has died.

key_terms.الدِّرْعِ: the garment covering the body during washing
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel; the circumstance in which the death occurs
key_terms.الْمَنْزِلَةِ: status or legal position in the ruling
key_terms.امْرَأَتُهُ: his wife; the spouse permitted to wash him
key_terms.زَوْجُهَا: her husband; the spouse who is excepted from the general ruling
key_terms.عَوْرَتِهَا: her private parts that must not be looked at
key_terms.يُغَسَّلُ: is to be given ghusl (ritual washing of the deceased)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a man or woman dies while traveling and only members of the opposite sex are present?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the ghusl of the deceased when a person dies in travel without same-gender attendants present. It states that in such cases the deceased is buried without ghusl, except that a spouse may perform the washing under specified restrictions, reflecting rulings related to modesty, death, and spousal permissibility.
